bull.b: AI demand is broad across Semiconductor Test, Product Test and Robotics rather than concentrated in one offering. This supports durable revenue expansion, improves cross-portfolio customer relevance, and creates opportunities to capture spending across the expanding AI infrastructure ecosystem.

High gross margins and sharply rising free cash flow give Teradyne resources to fund substantial R&D and capacity investment while preserving financial flexibility. Strong internal cash generation can support product leadership and customer programs through changing semiconductor demand conditions.

Very low leverage limits interest burden and refinancing exposure, leaving Teradyne better positioned to withstand semiconductor downturns. The conservative balance sheet also preserves capacity for R&D, capital investment, dividends, repurchases, or accretive acquisitions.

bear.b: Teradyne remains exposed to semiconductor and electronics capital-spending cycles, so demand can vary materially across device ramps and technology transitions. Uneven revenue and cash flow make earnings less predictable and can complicate capacity, inventory, and investment planning.

bear.t: Margin Pressure From Mix And Costs
bear.b: Even with strong current profitability, unfavorable product mix and rising ecosystem costs could limit margin expansion or reduce operating leverage. Capacity investment adds expense before demand fully matures, making sustained margin performance dependent on execution and revenue mix.

Robotics offers strategic growth but has less dependable near-term demand visibility beyond its largest customer. Reliance on turns and probabilistic opportunities can produce uneven segment revenue, while broader physical-AI adoption may take longer to convert into recurring scale.
